topics.title: Weather idioms
topics.intro_es: El inglés usa el clima para hablar de emociones, problemas y relaciones. Mira el dibujo: casi siempre te da una pista del significado.
topics.tip_es: No traduzcas los modismos palabra por palabra. Aprende cada uno con su situación típica y fíjate en la forma fija: steal someone’s thunder, be on cloud nine.

items.ex: Take a taxi — it’s raining cats and dogs out there!
I’m feeling a bit under the weather, so I’ll stay home.

items.es: una tormenta en un vaso de agua
items.ex: Their argument was just a storm in a teacup.
items.def: a lot of anger about something unimportant
items.note: US: a tempest in a teapot.

items.en: every cloud has a silver lining
items.es: no hay mal que por bien no venga
items.ex: I lost my job, but every cloud has a silver lining: now I can study.
items.def: something good comes out of every bad situation
items.form: every cloud has a silver lining

items.ex: She stole my thunder by announcing her news at my birthday party.
items.def: take attention or praise away from someone

items.es: estar en las nubes de felicidad
items.ex: Since he got the scholarship, he’s been on cloud nine.

items.en: have your head in the clouds
items.ex: He always has his head in the clouds during maths class.
items.def: not pay attention to what is happening

items.ex: The teacher played a game to break the ice on the first day.
items.def: make people feel relaxed when they first meet

items.ex: I can’t come tonight — can I take a rain check?
items.def: refuse an offer now but accept it later

items.ex: The small company managed to weather the storm of the crisis.

items.es: la calma antes de la tormenta
items.ex: The office was quiet — the calm before the storm of the sales season.
items.def: a quiet period before trouble starts

items.ex: Drink this tea and you’ll be as right as rain tomorrow.

items.es: estar hasta el cuello de trabajo
items.ex: I can’t go out this week; I’m snowed under with exams.

items.es: un amigo solo para los buenos momentos
items.ex: When I had problems, I discovered he was just a fair-weather friend.
items.def: a friend who disappears when you need help

items.ex: Let’s brainstorm some names for the new café.
items.def: suggest many ideas quickly in a group

items.ex: The exam was a breeze — I finished in twenty minutes.

topics.title: Climate change collocations
topics.intro_es: Las combinaciones de palabras que aparecen en cualquier noticia o ensayo sobre el clima. Apréndelas en bloque: cut emissions, no «reduce the emissions down».
topics.tip_es: Verbos que van con estos sustantivos: tackle climate change, reduce / cut emissions, switch to renewable energy, raise awareness.

items.ex: Global warming is making heatwaves more frequent.
Cars and factories release greenhouse gases.
We still depend on fossil fuels like oil and coal.
Flying less is the fastest way to reduce your carbon footprint.
Deforestation in the Amazon has reached record levels.
Rising sea levels threaten coastal cities like Cartagena.
Melting glaciers in the Andes put water supplies at risk.
Extreme weather events are becoming more common.
Biodiversity loss affects bees, birds and fish.
Governments promised to cut emissions by half by 2030.
Most of the country’s electricity comes from renewable energy.
La Guajira has great potential for wind power.
The university wants to be carbon-neutral by 2035.
We need a more sustainable way of producing food.
Some airlines let you offset the emissions of your flight.
Scientists warn that we are close to a tipping point.

topics.title: Urban planning & cityscapes
topics.intro_es: Para describir ciudades con precisión (como en la unidad «Exploring new cities»): cómo están organizadas, qué las hace vivibles y cómo cambian.
topics.tip_es: Bustling (positivo, lleno de vida) frente a overcrowded (negativo, demasiada gente). Quaint es encantador y antiguo, a veces un poco irónico.

figures.title: Shops in a city
figures.titleEs: De lo básico a lo avanzado en una ciudad

items.ex: The skyline of the city changes every year.
The new skyscraper has seventy floors.
The bridge has become the city’s most famous landmark.
The new stadium was built on the edge of the city.
The old industrial area is now full of art galleries.
Many families move to the suburbs for more space.
The airport is on the outskirts of the city.
The city centre is closed to cars on Sundays.
The mixed-use building has shops below and flats above.
The ring road takes traffic away from the centre.
The council has built forty kilometres of cycle lanes.
Building is not allowed in the green belt around the city.
Urban sprawl has swallowed the farms around the city.
Gentrification has pushed rents up in the old neighbourhood.
The regeneration project turned the old port into a park.
We had lunch in a bustling square full of street musicians.
Mexico City is a huge, sprawling metropolis.
Barichara is a quaint colonial town with stone streets.

topics.title: The fashion industry
topics.intro_es: Detrás de cada prenda hay diseñadores, fábricas, marcas y residuos. Vocabulario para debatir sobre la moda rápida y la moda sostenible.
topics.tip_es: Ojo: fashion es la industria y las tendencias; fashionable = de moda; in fashion / out of fashion. Mode no se usa para «moda».

items.ex: Fast fashion produces cheap clothes that people throw away quickly.
She only buys clothes with a designer label.
The brand opened a new store in Medellín.
The designer presented her autumn collection in Paris.
The models walked down the catwalk in silver boots.
Oversized jackets are the big trend this season.
Skinny jeans went out of fashion a few years ago.
That isn’t a real designer bag — it’s a cheap knock-off.
Many cheap T-shirts are made in sweatshops.
Garment workers protested about their working conditions.
Tonnes of textile waste end up in the desert in Chile.
All the cotton in this shirt is ethically sourced.
I buy most of my clothes second-hand.
I found this coat at a thrift store for ten dollars.
Upcycling turns old jeans into bags and jackets.
A capsule wardrobe has only a few pieces that all match.
